title: は 〜 が (topic + subject in one sentence)
meaning: The topic (は) is what you talk about; the subject (が) is what the predicate directly describes.
simpleExplanation: Many Japanese sentences have both は and が. は sets the big topic ("as for elephants"), and が marks the smaller subject that the description is really about ("the nose is long"): 象は鼻が長いです. English says "Elephants have long trunks"; Japanese says "As for elephants, the nose is long". You already use this shape in 私は寿司が好きです.
whenUsed: Describing a feature of a person, place or thing (Tanaka has big eyes, Tokyo has many people), and with likes, abilities and wants (私は〜が好きです／できます／ほしいです).
formation: Topic + は + Subject + が + Predicate

diagram.translation: Elephants have long trunks. (As for elephants, the nose is long.)

examples.reading: ぞうは はなが ながいです。
examples.en: Elephants have long trunks. (lit. As for elephants, the nose is long.)

examples.ja: 田中さんは目が大きいです。
examples.reading: たなかさんは めが おおきいです。
とうきょうは ひとが おおいです。
examples.en: Tokyo has a lot of people.

examples.reading: わたしは あたまが いたいです。
examples.en: I have a headache. (As for me, the head hurts.)
examples.note: Body parts and pain use は〜が.

examples.ja: この店はパンがおいしいです。
examples.reading: この みせは パンが おいしいです。

similarGrammar.difference: は alone marks the topic; here it combines with が.
が marks what the adjective directly describes.
The same は〜が shape: 私は寿司が好きです.

commonMistakes.why: Two は in one sentence means contrast, not description. The part described takes が.

commonMistakes.wrong: 象の鼻が長いです。(as a general description)
commonMistakes.why: Both are grammatical, but は〜が is the natural way to describe a feature of the topic.
The person is the topic (は); only the body part takes が.

usageNotes: Very common in N5 reading passages. The same structure underlies #29–#32 (私は犬が好きです). If the subject is a question word it always takes が: 誰が来ましたか — 田中さんが来ました.
jlptTips: In a sentence with two blanks like 田中さん（　）目（　）大きいです, the answer is は／が: big topic first, described part second.
Reading passages use this structure to describe people and towns. Read the が part as the real subject of the adjective.
